title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يحاضر بمنبر الجمعة عن "التعامل مع ظاهرة الجفاف؛ الأسباب والعلاج"
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures from the Friday Pulpit on "Dealing with the Phenomenon of Drought: Causes and Remedy"
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم ورئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين محاضرة علمية هامة تحت عنوان: "التعامل مع ظاهرة الجفاف؛ الأسباب والعلاج" بمنبر الجمعة في مسجد الذكر بتنسويلم مساء أمس الجمعة 25 رجب 1433هـ الموافق: 15 يونيو 2012م. وقد جرت المحاضرة وسط حضور جماهيري كبير غصت به جوانب المسجد وامتلأت به الساحات المحيطة به، حيث توافد الحضور من الساعات الأولى من المساء... وتوالى قدومهم حتى قبيل المغرب، إذ اكتظ داخل المسجد والساحات الموالية له، قبل أن يلجأ الجمهور إلى بعض الحيطان المجاورة، لينتظموا في جلوسهم متعطشين لحضور الشيخ والاستماع لما سيلقيه على آذانهم من العلم الشرعي، وتحرى الحضور حتى أمن على دعاء الشيخ في نهاية المحاضرة التي استمرت حتى دخول وقت المغرب. وقد استأنف فضيلة الشيخ حديثه في ابموضوع عن قدرة الله سبحانه وتعالى وتصرفه في الأمر كله، مذكرا أن الدار الدنيا محل الابتلاءات والامتحانات، وأن الظواهر الكونية من آيات الله تعالى التي يرسلها تخويفا وتذكيرا للمؤمنين، وذكر أن من أهم أسباب الجفاف ذنوب الخلق ومعاصيه، ومن حكمة الله تعالي تعجيل هذه المصائب لعباده في الدنيا للاعتبار والتذكير. ثم تكلم الشيخ عن منهج التعامل الكوني مع ظاهرة الجفاف، مذكرا بأن هذا الكون يحوي نواميس يدفع بعضها بعضا، وكما أن الدعاء من القدر، فإن القدر لا يرد إلا بالدعاء، "فالله سبحانه وتعالى من قدره أنه يسر لنا أسبابا تدفع هذه الكوارث، وهذه الأسباب تنقسم إلى قسمين: 1- أسباب عامة لكل الناس. 2- أسباب رسمية خاصة بذوي السلطان والقوة، وأهم هذه الأسباب الرسمية؛ تولية ولاة الأمر، أصحاب الحزم والعزم المقتدرين على حفظ الأمانات الصالحين الأكفاء". مستعرضا في ذلك العبر المستخلصة من قصة يوسف في توليه خزائن مصر، وخطته الاقتصادية في مواجهة السنوات العجاف التي مرت بها. واستخلص من ذلك عِبرا ومنهجا متكاملا في مواجهة الجفاف. وقد سرد الشيخ الكثير من النصوص الشرعية والأمثلة والعبر التي توجه وترشد في معالجة ظاهرة الجفاف التي تجتاح البلاد في هذه الآونة، ثم ختم بدعاء عظيم لعامة المسلمين وخاصتهم. لمتابعة المحاضرة اضغط هنا.
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, president of the Future Association for Calling to Islam, Culture and Education, and president of Abdullah ibn Yasin University — delivered an important scholarly lecture under the title "Dealing with the Phenomenon of Drought: Causes and Remedy" from the Friday pulpit at the Mosque of Remembrance in Tensweilim, on the evening of yesterday, Friday 25 Rajab 1433 AH, corresponding to 15 June 2012.

The lecture took place amid a large public attendance which filled the sides of the mosque to overflowing and filled the squares surrounding it. Those attending began arriving from the first hours of the evening... and continued to come until shortly before sunset, so that the inside of the mosque and the squares adjoining it were packed, before the crowd resorted to some of the neighbouring walls, arranging themselves in their seating, thirsting to be present with the Sheikh and to hear what he would deliver to their ears of the knowledge of the Sharia. Those present persevered to the point of saying amen to the Sheikh's supplication at the close of the lecture, which continued until the time of the sunset prayer came in.

The Sheikh resumed his talk on the subject with the power of God, glory be to Him and Most High, and His disposal of the whole affair, recalling that the abode of this world is the place of trials and of tests, and that the phenomena of the cosmos are among the signs of God Most High which He sends to instil fear and as a reminder to the believers. He mentioned that among the most important causes of drought are the sins and acts of disobedience of created beings, and that it is part of God Most High's wisdom (ḥikmah) to hasten these afflictions for His servants in this world, for the taking of a lesson and for a reminder.

The Sheikh then spoke about the method of dealing with the phenomenon of drought at the level of the created order, recalling that this cosmos contains laws which repel one another, and that just as supplication is part of what is decreed, so what is decreed is repelled only by supplication. "God, glory be to Him and Most High — it is part of what He has decreed that He has made available to us means which repel these catastrophes, and these means divide into two kinds: 1. General means, for all people. 2. Official means, particular to those possessed of authority and power; and the most important of these official means is the appointing to office of those in charge of affairs — men of resolve and determination, capable of safeguarding what is entrusted to them (amānāt), righteous and competent."

In that connection he reviewed the lessons drawn from the story of Joseph in his taking charge of the treasuries of Egypt, and his economic plan for confronting the lean years through which it passed; and from that he drew lessons and an integrated method for confronting drought.

The Sheikh set out many of the texts of the Sharia, the examples and the lessons that direct and guide in treating the phenomenon of drought which is sweeping the country at this time, and then closed with a mighty supplication for the Muslims, both the generality of them and the elect among them.

flags.arabic: أسباب رسمية خاصة بذوي السلطان والقوة، وأهم هذه الأسباب الرسمية؛ تولية ولاة الأمر، أصحاب الحزم والعزم المقتدرين على حفظ الأمانات الصالحين الأكفاء
flags.context: the second of the two kinds of means against drought, inside the record's only direct quotation of the Sheikh
options: render exactly, keeping the quotation marks the source supplies
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12. This is the one passage in the record that the source puts in quotation marks as the Sheikh's own words, and it is politically pointed: delivered in Nouakchott during the 2012 Sahel drought, it makes the appointment of resolute, trustworthy and competent officials the foremost official means of averting catastrophe. Read plainly it is a statement about good government offered as a religious remedy. It has been rendered exactly, with nothing softened and no gloss added; the publication decision is not the translator's. 'تولية ولاة الأمر' is rendered 'the appointing to office of those in charge of affairs' and is deliberately left as open as the Arabic, which does not say who does the appointing.

flags.arabic: وذكر أن من أهم أسباب الجفاف ذنوب الخلق ومعاصيه
options: among the most important causes of drought are the sins and acts of disobedience of created beings
one of the chief causes of drought is the sinning and disobedience of people
flags.note: Rendered exactly and neither softened nor sharpened: 'among the most important causes' is what the Arabic says, not 'the cause'. Two things matter for display. First, this is the news desk's compression of one strand of the lecture; the same record goes on to give the Sheikh a thoroughly practical remedy drawn from the Joseph narrative, and a reader who sees only this sentence sees half of his argument. Second, the sentence was spoken in a country then in drought, and in English on its own it reads as blaming the afflicted. The record should not be displayed with this line extractable from its second half. Note the source's own pronoun slip: a plural or collective subject (الخلق) with a singular possessive (معاصيه).

flags.arabic: كما أن الدعاء من القدر، فإن القدر لا يرد إلا بالدعاء
options: render as the report's prose and record the allusion
render with a hadith citation supplied
flags.note: An allusion to the widely circulated report 'nothing repels the decree but supplication' (narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others), given here without attribution or grading. Style guide section 4 forbids adding a grading the Sheikh did not give; none has been added, and the source gives none. Note also that the whole passage is creedal, turning on qadar — the decree — which style guide section 13 lists as a pending glossary addition and section 8 warns must not be read through the five legal rulings. Nothing here grades any act.

options: natural laws that push one against another
flags.note: nāmūs (pl. nawāmīs) is a Greek loanword used for a law of nature; the image is of one created regularity offsetting another, which is what licenses taking practical means against a decreed calamity. Rendered 'laws' with 'of the created order' supplied in the preceding sentence for 'الكوني'. Not in the glossary.

flags.context: وقد استأنف فضيلة الشيخ حديثه في ابموضوع عن قدرة الله
options: read as في الموضوع, 'on the subject'
flags.note: Source typo (ابموضوع for الموضوع). Preserved and flagged. The same record also writes تعالي for تعالى, an ordinary Egyptian-keyboard yāʾ substitution, left as served.

flags.arabic: وقد جرت المحاضرة وسط حضور جماهيري كبير ... حتى دخول وقت المغرب
flags.context: the second paragraph, against the second paragraph of record 795
flags.note: Word-for-word identical with the corresponding paragraph of record 795, a different lecture five weeks earlier at the same mosque, but for a stray ellipsis here. It is house boilerplate, not observation of this evening. Translated in full, as the style guide requires, and flagged so that the site does not present it as a report of this occasion.

translator_notes: A news-desk report of a lecture, with one short passage quoted directly. The lecture itself exists only as a recording that the record points to and the corpus does not hold.
The CMS timestamp, 16 June 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body dates the lecture to the evening of Friday 25 Rajab 1433 / 15 June 2012.
The story referred to is the Qur'anic narrative of Joseph and the seven lean years (Sūrat Yūsuf 12:43–57); the record names neither sura nor verses and none has been inserted.
'عامة المسلمين وخاصتهم' is rendered 'the generality of them and the elect among them' — a standing pair in Arabic supplication, covering ordinary believers and those of particular standing.
